chapters.title: The Sealed Lamp and the Road Home
warnings: fluency-02: output near-identical to base — copied, not re-voiced

chapters.title: The God No Pointing Can Reach
comprehension_flags: *Suradiq* is used as the name of a structural division ("the first canopy of light") without explanation, and a modern reader may not grasp that it labels a section of the book.
terminology_notes: Arabic technical terms — the source alternates between backtick styling (`yustaftahu`) and italic styling (*fataha*) for transliterations; one convention should be chosen book-wide.

chapters.title: The Sin of Naming the Unnameable
editorial_queries: "Sayyidna Muayyad" is used both for the author quoted (identified as Hibatullah ibn Musa al-Shirazi) and, within the same clause, for Mawlana Sayyidna Muayyad al-Din his spiritual father, leaving unclear which figure each earlier attribution names.
comprehension_flags: The passage states "Ten ranks in all" yet the ascending ladder as listed names more than ten stations, which a reader may struggle to reconcile.
terminology_notes: "Sayyidna Muayyad" — the two distinct bearers (al-Shirazi and al-Din) should be disambiguated consistently across the book.

chapters.title: What Oneness Actually Means
terminology_notes: marifat / marifah — the same word appears in two transliterated forms (*marifat al-hudud* versus *marifah zahirah* / *marifah batinah*); a book-wide decision on whether to unify the spelling would keep the technical term uniform on every occurrence.

chapters.title: The Nearest Rank: Breaking the Self to Climb
comprehension_flags: "the knowledge of the Tenth" and "the commands of the Tenth" name a specific figure the passage never identifies, and a general reader will not know whom "the Tenth" refers to.
terminology_notes: وَلِيّ — rendered "friend" in the narration but "Wali" inside the quoted gloss; a book-wide decision should fix one English form for this term.

chapters.title: Every Teacher a Threshold, Not a God
comprehension_flags: The closing cascade of ranks (ashir, Adam the summoner, Qaims, Dais, Hujjats, Imams, the circle of ain, the circle of mim) arrives with no gloss, and a general reader will not know what these named ranks are or how they order.
terminology_notes: the Originator — rendered once as "mubdi-e taala" (a Persian/Urdu construct) but elsewhere as "the mubdi" and "the Originator"; one transliteration should be standardized book-wide.

Kitab al-Alim wa al-Ghulam, "the Book of the Master and the Disciple" — this English rendering collides with the standard scholarly translation of that title and should be standardized book-wide, likely with a distinguishing subtitle.

chapters.title: Out of Nothing, and Equal in Justice
editorial_queries: In the going-astray pair, the base verb is written زَلَّ ("he went astray") against the causative أَضَلَّ, but أَضَلَّ is the causative of ضَلَّ — the source may carry a ز/ض script error, and it has been reproduced verbatim rather than corrected.
terminology_notes: "first perfection" / "second perfection" (kamal al-awwal / kamal al-thani) should be standardized to these exact renderings book-wide, as the whole justice argument turns on the pair.

chapters.title: The First to Say There Is No God But He
comprehension_flags: The sentence "The First Intellect came to be, the Originator made seven, and the tenth is the ashir — but the luminous world stopped at seven" introduces a "tenth" (ashir) with no prior referent, so a modern reader cannot reconcile the count of seven with the mention of a tenth.
